newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Afghan city starts clean-up after munitions blast.
newsitem.headline: Afghan city starts clean-up after munitions blast.

text.p: A clean-up operation began on Friday at the scene of a munitions dump explosion that killed or wounded more than 300 people in the eastern Afghan city of Jalalabad.
Relief workers say nearly 300 people were wounded in the Wednesday's blast at the Islamic Taleban militia's security department headquarters in a western district of the city.
Estimates of the death toll vary widely. The Taleban say 10 died, while residents say they believe more than 100 people lost their lives. U.N. officials have put the toll at 30.
U.N. battle area clearance teams collected more than 400 unexploded artillery shells and mortar bombs in the first two hours of the clean-up operation, witnesses said.

The blast scattered unexploded ordnance over a four-km (1-1/2-mile) square area, cutting a swathe of destruction, according to Stefan Kuhnehellemessen of the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies.
"Twenty-two houses were completely destroyed and 64 partially destroyed -- at least they have a room or so left," Kuhnehellemesen said.
He said the federation was distributing relief supplies to blast victims.

"We started distribution last night of tents to families whose houses have been completely destroyed. Yesterday we also distributed cooking pots and kerosene and blankets for some 60 families," he said.
Kuhnehellemesen said five people had been killed and 45 wounded in one extended family alone.
The United Nations has brought in 130 men to clear the site of the explosion and make it safe.
On Friday morning, U.N. teams were walking in widely spaced lines, each man carrying a mortar bomb to collection points.
"We collect the shells without fuses and take them away. A few fused shells will be destroyed where they lie," said Noel Spencer, a U.N. technical adviser on mine clearance.
Ambulances were standing by in case of an accident. On Thursday, a man died when an artillery shell blew up on the ground.
Residents were starting to reconstruct their mud brick houses. One old man was picking bricks out of the rubble of his home and piling them up before starting to rebuild.
